a.text: Just before the mother engaged the dark mist, the wakeman of the woods came to remind her that she had yet to do that which was most important: hold a proper funeral for her daughter.

The mother had intended to fight the dark mist to the death, but tears began to stream down her face when the wakeman sang their ancient song, and she chose to follow tradition and hold a wake for her daughter.

All through the night she cried at the purple bonfire representing her daughter's soul. The downpour of tears quenched the fire burning through the city, nearly extinguishing even the purple funeral fire.
When the wakeman once again asked the mother if she would still fight the dark mist to the death, she gazed upon the smoldering bonfire with tears on her face, saying,
As she said those words, the feeble purple flame suddenly turned bright yellow. Her daughter rose from death and walked out of the flames, and mother and daughter embraced each other.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: So ends the story. Not in fragments, but a true...

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: ...ending.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Congratulations. We've pieced together the truth.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: And what a happy ending!

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: This is all thanks to you! Come, let us toast, then I'll write this all down and publish it for—

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: Well, publishing it may be a, uh, a challenge. But now that it's complete—

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: The funeral, the bonfire, the resurrection... you saw everything.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: I never expected you to find the courage to return to Na Saoirsí.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Singer.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: And it was a lovely ending, wasn't it? Eblana departed with the dead, never to return.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: As for you, Your Highness Loughshinny, I dedicate this story to you. Whether to publish it, seal it away, or have it fade into obscurity along with the remnants of Dublinn like me—is all up to you.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: How wonderful.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: I almost regret allowing you to belittle yourself with a title like The Singer.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: You—

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Wait, what?!

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: You're not Loughshinny. Y-You're—Eblana?!
The once 'Singer' swings his arm furiously, spilling his drink on the table.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: You're dead! You can't be alive! You were killed, twice! Once by spear, and once by fire—you shouldn't be here!

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Or am I dead? Ha, haha... this isn't funny. You're dead, Red Dragon! Go back to where you belong!

spans.text: dead? Ha, haha... this isn't funny. You're dead, Red Dragon! Go back to where you belong!

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: I see. That's it. It was all a lie. You never died. You killed Loughshinny instead. It was all a trick, an illusion—

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: If so, what becomes of your story?

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: My... story?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Have you calmed down?

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: You shouldn't be alive... no...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Has death ever been an eternal sleep for me? What I could do with life, I can do with death.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: As a reward for completing the story, 'Writer', let me tell you one thing: All that matters is fire.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: ...The purple fire.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The purple fire from your story. It may seem ethereal, but it is no fiction.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: It is true that, over the long course of the war, I shared too much of my flame with others and became weak, feeble.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: But fire spreads. Fire consumes. Fire grows.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: After the battle with the Nachzehrer on the Gastrell, I needed to take back the flames I had given away, which had been growing on the plains, in the ruins, in the hearts of the people.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: You wanted it repaid... with interest.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Taxation is the most basic authority of a monarch.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Mundane kings collect blood taxes to nurture their armies, to fight over land and people that will last mere centuries at most.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I collect blood taxes to pave a road between life and death with the Red Dragon's flame, so that all those caught in between will look up to me.

spans.text: collect blood taxes to pave a road between life and death with the Red Dragon's flame, so that all those caught in between will look up to me.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: The ravings of a madwoman...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: No doubt it sounds that way to you, for you cannot fathom what happens when enough death to consume a nation is returned to its master.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: A thousand years of anger, sorrow, and hatred converged on me all at once. Did you think they would let my flesh and spirit fade away so easily?

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: A slave to hatred. What a fitting end for you—

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Have you already forgotten what I said in your story?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Everyone—and everything—that thought they could mold me just happened to take on a form I was able to wield with ease.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Were I truly their slave, you'd have been ash the moment I saw you.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: ...You lunatic!

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: That's why you allowed Wellington to station his troops in the Dark Woods, to blockade the city, even continued the curfew... You never intended to spare Na Saoirsí!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Why thank you for finally being willing to shed light on the unpleasant truth of the dark mist and Wellington.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Does the Battle of Silverrock Bluffs, which you witnessed from the deck of the Gastrell, still haunt you in your alcohol-fueled dreams?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: It's never left you, has it? Why else would you be so obsessed with depicting the mist dangling above people's heads, yet so loathe to define it?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The curfew was justified at first. There were still Victorian spies in Na Saoirsí at the time indeed.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The Duke of Wellington stepped up the blockade when Loughshinny entered the city, because he wanted to smother any possibility of news leaking about the two red dragons.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: And the food that disappeared and came back on its own...

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: The Brigadier was more than just your most trusted lieutenant—he was also captain of Wellington's Redsteel Guard. When he went to ask for supplies, Wellington acquiesced.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Wellington simply became disappointed in Loughshinny when she left Na Saoirsí to seek the wakemen, that's all.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You should thank her, really. You'd never have escaped the woods if Wellington hadn't relaxed the blockade out of disappointment.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: As for the victory party you were so afraid to describe...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Don't tell me you've really glorified it into a fairy tale in your memories?

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Of course not...

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: What happened to the Dublinners who weren't willing to give up their power, the ones you took away on a pretext?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: They were 'swallowed by the dark mist,' as you put it. Quite literally.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: But Loughshinny still managed to make up her mind and killed you, and Wellington didn't follow your ridiculous orders!

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Suppose I believe that your aberrant purple fire left you a vessel. What do you plan to do with it? Lead an army of the dead to retake Tara?

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: I won't help you. No living soul will. You and your dead friends can go straight to hell!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Indeed, you were never suited to be Dublinn's Singer.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You cling to what you see and believe. When the two could no longer be reconciled, you chose self-destruction rather than to give up on either.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: But do you really imagine that everything has gone the way you think?

steps.name: Solemn Servant
steps.text: A letter, Your Grace.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: You may enter.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Is it urgent?

steps.name: Solemn Servant
steps.text: N-No, ma'am.

steps.name: Solemn Servant
steps.text: But look at the seal. It corresponds to no emblem on record from the past fifty years...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Tara?
The Duke of Caster scrutinizes what the servant is holding.
On the edge of the envelope is an emblem excavated from the dusts of history.
The young have never seen it, while the old have forgotten it. Only those forced to keep an eye on history remember its source.

steps.name: Solemn Servant
steps.text: We are uncertain whether it is the mark of Tara... or of King Gaeil.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I never took you for a scholar of heraldry.

steps.name: Solemn Servant
steps.text: That was not my intention. I just—

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: It is enough that we know what it signifies.
'To the Duke of Caster.'

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Open it and read it out aloud.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Not too quickly.

steps.name: Solemn Servant
steps.text: Yes, ma'am.

steps.name: Solemn Servant
steps.text: There is no greeting...

a.text: 'The response was delayed as the time was not yet ripe. Now, it is.'
'From this day forth, martial law is hereby lifted in Na Saoirsí and the surrounding lands south of the Grey Hills...'

steps.name: Newsboy
steps.text: Extra! Extra! Read all about it!

steps.name: Newsboy
steps.text: Martial law to be lifted at midnight across all of Tara!

steps.name: Newsboy
steps.text: Publishing restrictions lifted! The art community rejoices! Read more on page two—

steps.name: Leisurely Resident
steps.text: Finally. Now we can call this a proper tavern.

steps.name: Barkeeper
steps.text: Hear, hear! With the curfew lifted, you can drink all through the night!

steps.name: Barkeeper
steps.text: Besides, it's my birthday! Drinks are on the house!

steps.name: Leisurely Resident
steps.text: R-Really?

steps.name: Leisurely Resident
steps.text: You sure about this? There are enough people in the city to drink you out of house and home.

steps.name: Barkeeper
steps.text: Worry about yourself. Look at you, rich boy, leaving your lamp on in the middle of the day!

steps.name: Leisurely Resident
steps.text: Tch, I was just so busy I forgot.

steps.name: Leisurely Resident
steps.text: It's been warm lately, so I've been renovating. Thought I'd take the day off. Guess I really have been too busy.

steps.name: Leisurely Resident
steps.text: So how about another beer? I've got to get this fatigue out of my system.

steps.name: Barkeeper
steps.text: Here you go.

steps.name: Leisurely Resident
steps.text: On the other hand, I'm almost more afraid of not being tired. Being tired is how I know I'm still breathing—no, that's not quite it. How should I put this—

spans.text: On the other hand, I'm almost more afraid of
being tired. Being tired is how I know I'm still breathing—no, that's not quite it. How should I put this—

steps.name: Barkeeper
steps.text: Living.

steps.name: Leisurely Resident
steps.text: Yes, living.

steps.name: Barkeeper
steps.text: You too, ma'am, here's one for you—

steps.name: Barkeeper
steps.text: Oh, it's you, Emma.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: I'm sorry. I've got to get going.

steps.name: Barkeeper
steps.text: Off to do your time on the ag plate?

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Barkeeper
steps.text: No idea how you managed to smuggle all that food out last year, but I hear you've been paying it off with honest work over there. So no need to be shy now, have one on me.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: Thank you...

steps.name: Leisurely Resident
steps.text: To living.

steps.name: Barkeeper
steps.text: To Tara.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: To...
Emma holds the cup with one hand and puts the other in her pocket, clutching the necklace she reclaimed last winter.
The words said to her when it was returned come out of her mouth almost by instinct.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: ...To all our countrymen who gave their lives for Tara.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: You're really leaving, Brigid?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Yeah, the burdenbeasts are callin' for me from their pastures.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Besides, still haven't been to this 'Rhodes Island' that Loughshinny wanted me to see. Want to come with?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Maybe if I have the chance.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: It's just sad to think that you're the one who brought us to Na Saoirsí, but can't stay yourself.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: It's not that I couldn't, I just chose not to. Like your own choice to stay.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Say hi to the wakemen for me, if they come back to the city.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Is that your intuition again?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: It's not always right.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: But I don't smell that burning stink anymore. Smells like fresh buds in spring, dew in the morning.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Hello, Brigadier.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You two know each other?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: You could say that.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: What are you doing here? I don't recall anything happening which the Redsteel Guard would need to be deployed for.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: I'm on leave. I came to honor the memory of my comrades... scoundrels, to be sure, but they fought by my side.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: If you're looking to take revenge for those who died during your exile, this is your chance. A brawl with a soldier on leave wouldn't be considered an attack on the military.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: ...It wasn't you who killed Selmon and the others. Not directly.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I'll remember what you did. That's enough for me.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: What more can anyone ask for, than to be remembered?

a.text: '...Bealtaine, also known as the Festival of Fire, is scheduled to be revived in the coming days.'
'The fire-passing ritual will start in Oak Grove County.'

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: You're awfully quiet. Are you nervous?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: No, it just strikes me that we managed to turn what you'd see in the books into reality.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: On the last day of spring, we extinguish the fires in our homes, then come together to relight them at Bealtaine. In the smoke of the bonfire and drifting ash...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: We welcome the coming of a new season, and of a new life.

steps.name: A Voice
steps.text: Your Highness Loughshinny, the lighting ceremony will begin in a few minutes—

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Alright, thank you.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Maybe I've waited too long for this. It feels no realer than a dream.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I wanted to sing, Nemos, but you've already sung for me back in Na Saoirsí... So this time, the flames in my hand will do the singing.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: One more thing, Your Highness... about Her Highness Eblana—

steps.name: A Voice
steps.text: Your Highness! It's time!

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Sorry, Nemos. We can speak after the ritual.
The Draco steps forward.
A stone platform, sculpted in the style of the ruins, serves as her lectern. She lights the bonfire upon it, and turns around.
From the square below her, many faces gaze up with bated breath.
She takes a deep breath.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: A thousand years ago, the Dracos of Victoria invaded Tara, creating the title of King Gaeil as an epithet of shame, robbing the nomadic Tarans of their freedom.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Six hundred years ago, the reigning King Gaeil had no choice but to allow the Victorians to remake the royal capital in their own image.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Two hundred years ago, the Aslans seized the crown of Victoria, but once again they trampled the dreams of the Tarans beneath their feet, such that even our language was almost lost to us.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Now, Tara stands on her own.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I recite this history of shame, not to fan the flames of hatred, but in defense of peace.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Sing what songs in Victorian suffice to praise the beauty you see.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Tell what tales in Taran will move the passions.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: We remember so that we might provide the living the dignity of life, and the dead the promise of reunion.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Throughout the cold night...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: We shall retain a warm flame.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: As such, I, Loughshinny Dublinn, the last descendent of the Taran Dracos...

a.text: 'I shall light this fire symbolizing new life. May it guide the way for all, whether living or departed.'

steps.name: Solemn Servant
steps.text: 'Enclosed you will find templates for nomadic city immigration forms.'

steps.name: Solemn Servant
steps.text: Signed... 'The Kingdom of Tara'.

steps.name: Solemn Servant
steps.text: This is... This is treason.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: The King of Tara has long been one of the titles of the Victorian emperor. Nothing in this letter denies it.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: To avoid conflict, the Red Dragon has even indefinitely delayed the 'coronation' so many are looking forward to.

steps.name: Solemn Servant
steps.text: But in reality...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: In reality, the indecisive claimant, the corrupt oligarchs, the blockading army, and the flames of dissent... all these issues have been put to rest.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: For the first time in centuries, they proudly tell a new legend of a King Gaeil.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: In the short term, the unrest has indeed been contained within Wellington's domain. With time, however, it can become a greater threat than any insurrection.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Tara must not be allowed to secede from Victoria.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: As long as Wellington doesn't take his entire territory away on a nomadic city, the other dukes and I will continue negotiating with him.

steps.name: Solemn Servant
steps.text: Yes, ma'am. I'll draft some long terms plans regarding that.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Phew... It's finally over...

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Well done. Well done indeed.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: So what was it you wanted to say about Eblana before the ceremony?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: We never found her body. If she somehow survived, I worry that someday...

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Someday a completely different story will be told about the resurrection of the Red Dragon.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What story? That it was no miracle, but the assassination of one dragon by another?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Worse than that.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I see. You're afraid that Eblana will return and paint the whole thing as a conspiracy I orchestrated.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Our position is not unassailable.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: We both know that her body disappeared earlier that night, after you killed her the first time. What I dragged through the streets wasn't her body, but an empty coffin.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I also know that it was I who used the last spark of fire she left in her spear to ignite the coffin.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: It was I who left the city to parlay with Wellington, laying out our plans in exchange for him delaying military action while they played out.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: It was I who walked into the fire the people had returned to Eblana, I who quenched and replaced the fire of death with the fire of life, and I who walked out of the fire in the end.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: We've known all this since that day on the balcony of Na Saoirsí's citadel.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Eblana had left us a puzzle with no solution. The only way out was a miracle.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: A miracle we scripted and directed.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: If anything, the true miracle was the wakemen returning to the city.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: If Eblana hadn't awakened the Exiled King, if Brigid hadn't delivered that message centuries overdue, if Moran hadn't persuaded them...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: With just the two of us, that miracle could never have occurred.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: So, what is there to fear at this point?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Eblana has cut off any path leading away from the throne. All I can do is devote the rest of my days to Tara.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: And patiently await my judgment in some unknowable future.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Nemos was dragging an empty coffin?! Loughshinny was planning to 'resurrect the dragon' the moment she first killed you?

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: You're lying! You—

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: I know! It was Wellington! He found a conscience and lifted the blockade on his own!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You just won't give up, will you?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The Iron Duke? With a conscience? Hilarious.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: You promised him that only good could come of your scheming!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: All I promised him on the Gastrell was that I could change the direction of Tara, so long as Loughshinny was willing to return.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The Red Dragon who breathes flames of death, the spectre force with its dead soldiers, Dublinn with its blood-stained hands... everything was fated to sink into darkness while the Tarans united under the banner of the one and only Red Dragon.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Of course, His Grace was unaware that everyone in Na Saoirsí was meant to die for the plan, but I knew.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: A city of doomed souls in exchange for Tara's lasting stability. Only good could come of it, no?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: A shame that the duke isn't fond of Loughshinny. Things could have gone even more smoothly otherwise.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Sophistry! You lied to Wellington! Your plan was anything but harmless! And the people of Na Saoirsí did live!

spans.text: Sophistry! You lied to Wellington! Your plan was anything but harmless! And the people of Na Saoirsí

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: To everyone's surprise.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: In exchange for their lives, Loughshinny reached for the scepter of power that she detested so much. She chose to write a saga, a novel, a miracle that should have been beneath her noble dignity.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: It was something only she could do... something that wouldn't have been possible even a few years ago. Would you have placed a miracle on the scales from the start?

spans.text: It was something only she could do... something that wouldn't have been possible even a few years ago. Would
have placed a miracle on the scales from the start?

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: What if Loughshinny had failed?!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Then you wouldn't be sitting here enjoying your drink.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I'm sure you've heard stories about what the Iron Duke does to whatever he considers an obstacle.
Every story begins with an inspiration. Memories rush into the writer's mind like seawater at high tide.
He struggles to break free, only to find himself powerless against the oncoming tide.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Argh—ugh! *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Red Dragon...

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: You knew! You knew from the beginning!

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Y-You almost destroyed Na Saoirsí! You've made a mockery of all Tara!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Now, now, I must object to that. I simply fulfilled a promise. Is being true to one's word no longer a virtue?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Even you yourself admitted that this was a 'happy ending'.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: No—never! This isn't how the story ends—

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: This isn't how my story's supposed to go!
The writer sees a sliver of white. He falls to his knees and crawls along the ground, trying to collect the scattered sheets of paper that had flown loose.
One, two, three... He clutches them in his hand along with his pen.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: No, no, no—

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: What would you like to write? Let me help you.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: No—

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: NOOOO!
The writer's shoulders tremble hysterically. Panicked, he begins to back off, until his back hits the rickety wall of the tavern.
Grabbing his pen like a spear, he begins to stab at the paper.
Muttering under his breath, he only manages to cover them with scattered ink blots. Soon, even his muttering loses coherence.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Gah... brr... argh... ugh! Ugh!
The commotion causes the drunken barkeep to come out from behind the counter and grab him by the collar.

steps.name: Brusque Barkeep
steps.text: Wha'cha babblin' about?

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Argh! Eh... ugh!
Realizing that he can no longer form words, the writer looks desperately towards the woman watching him with disinterest.
He points at the woman's hands, then at his own mouth. The meaning was clear.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You've lost your words.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Perhaps you hit your head from excitement, or had a minor stroke.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Or perhaps it's because you just saw something you believed in so firmly, for so long, shatter to pieces.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The very thing that inspired you to join Dublinn, caused you to stay at the victory party, made you turn back to Na Saoirsí halfway...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: But it's time to wake up.
With a trembling hand, the writer tries to write on his palm, but leaves only crooked, disjointed lines.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You wrote a story for Tara. A complete story, not a collection of fragments. It's a good one. I like it.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: And I like it even more now that it belongs only to me, not to you.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Slán go fóill, 'Singer'. No, 'Writer'.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Slán go fóill, the last Dublinner.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I look forward to the stories you'll tell me when death reunites us.
With one last glance at The Writer, the woman tosses a few coins onto the table, and walks out of the tavern.
A memory comes back to The Writer.

It was the same look Eblana gave him that night, a year and a half ago, when he decided to delay his report after The Leader's shadow had already departed, in hopes of staying in both sides' good graces.

options: What should I call you, then?

steps.text: Whatever you're thinking, I am only Necrass here.
Unless you, too, find a signed sheet of paper to hold no power whatsoever.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: If you find the title necessary, Erudite.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: For my part, I'm more curious about your lack of reaction upon hearing the whole story.

options: I read the report on Na Saoirsí.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: Ah. A lapse on my part, I see.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: First a private letter from Na Saoirsí, then fragments through official channels... Loughshinny is getting better at this.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: Then I presume she's told you all about me, which is why you were willing to sit down with me by yourself, and hear out this patchwork tale of allusions and insinuations.

options: No, she has yet to 'find your body.'
She's unaware you're in a position to tell stories.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: That makes your courage all the more admirable.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: And I mustn't neglect to give credit to Loughshinny where it's due. She's more than just a qualified dance partner now—she's ready to take the lead. I do hope she enjoys herself.

options: Sounds like you like your new powers.
Sounds like you like your new toy.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: Of course I do. The powers of the dead aren't necessarily greater than those of the living, but they are more lasting, and harder to check.

options: But you'll soon grow bored of them.
Like everything else you've ever had.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: Life is short, but death is long, Erudite.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: There are still so many interesting people in the mortal realm. That alone is reason enough for me to await them in death.

options: So you gave Reed your old toys?

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: A cutting question, Erudite. But I'll allow it.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: And not only because your accusation is astute, if prejudiced. But also because you are one of the interesting people I mentioned.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: Must everything be done for a purpose?

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: I am inseparable from death. Is it not the natural order of things that those like me should be drawn to Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: I was drawn, so I came. This place is always covered in the scent of death, after all—especially around you, my dear Erudite.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: You will, someday.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: When the tides erupt and the night of death descends, you will be grateful for my presence, so long as I do not mock your predicament.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: As for right now?

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: I am simply the shadow of Tara's leader.

steps.name: Necrass
steps.text: Just Necrass, nothing more.
